headline: Kept five zoning amendments in committee after public hearings on parking maximums, ground story elevations, accessory dwelling units, principal entrances, and terminology.
summary: Public hearings were held on five zoning amendments requested by the Mayor. The amendments cover parking maximums, ground story elevation requirements, accessory dwelling unit rules to align with State Law, principal entrance requirements, and terminology for affordable dwelling units and commercial spaces. All five were kept in committee, and public comments will be accepted until Friday October 30th, 2026, at 12:00 PM.
decisions: Kept the amendment to correct parking maximums (ID # 26-1258) in committee; no vote recorded.
Kept the amendment to remove ground story elevation requirements (ID # 26-1259) in committee; no vote recorded.
Kept the amendment to align with State Law on protected accessory dwelling units (ID # 26-1336) in committee; no vote recorded.
Kept the amendment to clarify requirements for principal entrances (ID # 26-1337) in committee; no vote recorded.
Kept the amendment to update terminology for affordable dwelling units and commercial spaces (ID # 26-1338) in committee; no vote recorded.

Planner clarified under state law that the city cannot have a more restrictive height limit, but the square footage is malleable.

requirement be added that an owner be required to show proof of proper permit processes followed and tenants notified appropriately.
